recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not reintroduce the longer FHIR-27753 examples unless Pharmacy reopens or reverses the later FHIR-54903 wording decision.
issue_request: FHIR-27753 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy technical correction for R5. It reported that MedicationRequest status entered-in-error had usage notes but no actual definition, and asked to add a definition before those notes; the accepted resolution supplied wording beginning 'The prescription was recorded against the wrong patient or for some reason should not have been recorded'.
initial_application: The seed was applied in git commit 76ef92c3597ed1e3e2e1e7e398e6e772f385df64, which changed source/medicationrequest/codesystem-medicationrequest-status.xml from notes-only text to the accepted FHIR-27753 definition-plus-notes wording.
additional_context: FHIR-54903 is a later Applied/Persuasive Pharmacy issue that explicitly changed the MedicationRequest entered-in-error definition from the FHIR-27753 wording to 'The request was entered in error and is not valid.' Git commit 358c5eb203b35c6326e060566926db8aeda12352 applied that later decision, and Pharmacy minutes for 2026-03-02 record the FHIR-54903 vote. The original Zulip thread confirms the seed concern was the lack of a clear definition before usage notes.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/medicationrequest/codesystem-medicationrequest-status.xml defines entered-in-error as 'The request was entered in error and is not valid.', which provides the direct definition requested by FHIR-27753 while respecting the later FHIR-54903 decision to simplify the wording.
